title: History 13: Seeing in 3D: NeRF, Gaussian splats and structured latents
hook: Ask a network for every point on every ray, or just draw blobs? How 3D went from one to the other, then to sparse latents.

verified.claim: NeRF's input is a 5D coordinate and its outputs are volume density and view-dependent radiance, projected with classic volume rendering.
SLAT combines a sparse 3D grid with dense multiview visual features and decodes to radiance fields, Gaussians and meshes.
NerfEmbedder in Chroma Radiance adds a 2D positional encoding to image patches, so it has nothing to do with 3D.
RenderSplat composites front to back through depth slabs.
The lab's three-slice result matches a hand calculation.
The graph passes validate_prompt with file menus skipped.

unchecked: We could not extract text from the NeRF PDF in this session, so the lab's sum is the standard emission-absorption form, labelled as such. We confirmed from the abstract only that NeRF uses classic volume rendering.
The 192 samples in the cost line is an example number we picked. We did not confirm the paper's sample counts.
We ran no 3D model for this lesson. No 3D checkpoint is on our test machine.
The real-time claim for splats is the paper's own, and we did not time it.
